tool.name: SlopeZonalStatisticsAsTable

summary.para: Summarizes a slope raster per zone into a table: count, mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, range, 5th/95th percentiles, and the 95% confidence interval of the mean slope. Very similar to Esri's Zonal Statistics as Table tool, but targeted specifically at slope rasters -- the mean, SD and CI are computed on the slope angles and converted back to the raster's unit for display -- and it requires no Spatial Analyst or Image Analyst extension.

tool.usage:
Relation to the Esri tool. This tool deliberately mirrors Esri's Zonal Statistics as Table (Spatial Analyst / Image Analyst): zones come from an integer raster or from features, all cells sharing a zone value are summarized together, and the result is a standalone table with one row per zone. It differs in three ways. First, the moment statistics are computed in angle space: terrain steepness is an angle, and percent slope is its tangent -- a convex transform -- so averaging raw percent values biases the mean and every derived statistic high (half a landscape at 50 degrees and half at 70 degrees averages 60 degrees; averaging the same cells as 119% and 274% gives 197% = 63 degrees, which is wrong). Percent, ratio, and gradian values pass through the arctangent before the mean/SD/CI, and single-value results convert back to the source unit for display (the reported mean is the tangent of the mean angle, never the mean of the tangents). The average steepness of a landscape does not depend on the unit it was measured in. Second, options that do not fit (majority/minority/variety, multidimensional processing, the output join layer) are omitted. Third, it needs no extension: everything is computed internally, so it runs on any ArcGIS Pro license.
Slope units. The drop-down names the unit of the input raster: degrees (-90 to 90), percent slope (100 × rise/run, so 45 degrees = 100%), rise:run ratio, or gradians (100 gon = 90 degrees). It defaults automatically from the raster's geoprocessing history (Esri's Slope and Surface Parameters tools record DEGREE or PERCENT_RISE in the metadata lineage), falling back to degrees when nothing can be determined -- always check it. All single-value outputs (mean, median, min, max, range, percentiles, CI bounds) are reported in this unit; the standard deviation and the CI half-width are reported in degrees, because a dispersion has no exact nonlinear conversion.
Negative slopes. Some slope datasets are signed (a directional pitch along a route, for example). The "Treat negative slopes as positive" option (checked by default) takes the absolute value first, giving statistics on absolute steepness; unchecked, values keep their sign, so downhill can balance uphill in the mean. Either way, each zone's count of originally negative values is reported in NEG_COUNT, so signed data always announces itself. Values outside the valid range for the chosen unit (beyond +/-90 degrees or +/-100 gon; percent and ratio are unbounded) are excluded, counted, and reported with a might-not-be-a-slope-raster warning.
Zones. All features sharing the same value in the zone field -- or all raster cells sharing the same integer value -- form one zone. Zone rasters must be integer rasters in the same coordinate system as the slope raster. Feature zones are processed one zone at a time, each over its own window of the slope raster, so zones that overlap are each analyzed in full (the historic rasterize-first overlap problem cannot occur); within a single zone, overlapping features count each cell once. Polygon zones use every cell whose center falls inside; polyline zones use every cell the line passes through; point zones interpolate the slope at each point bilinearly, computed on the slope angles of the four surrounding cell centers. Integer, text, GUID, and ObjectID fields all make valid zone fields (choosing the ObjectID makes every feature its own zone). If Ignore NoData is unchecked, any zone containing a NoData cell receives NULL statistics, matching the Esri tool.
The 95% confidence interval of the mean uses the t distribution (Zar 1999 ch. 7; exact through 30 degrees of freedom). With very many cells the interval is extremely narrow -- that is real precision, not an error. The output table's metadata records the inputs and settings (provenance), and the tool prints a ready-to-run Python snippet so the run can be scripted. No Spatial Analyst or Image Analyst extension is required. See also this toolbox's Aspect Zonal Statistics as Table (the circular sibling of this tool) and the Slope Graphic tool (a visual version of these statistics).

param.name: in_zone_data
param.displayname: Input raster or feature zone data

dialogReference.para: The zones: an integer raster (each distinct value is a zone) or a point, polyline, or polygon feature class or layer. An active selection on a layer is honored. Overlapping features in different zones are each analyzed in full; overlapping features in the same zone count each cell once.

The field defining the zones: features sharing the same value form one zone. Integer, text, GUID, and ObjectID fields are all accepted (choosing the ObjectID makes every feature its own zone). Required for feature zones; a zone raster always uses its cell value (the field defaults to Value).

The slope raster to summarize, in the unit named below. Any pixel type is accepted. Values outside the valid range for the unit (beyond +/-90 degrees or +/-100 gon) are excluded, counted, and reported.

The output table: one row per zone, holding the zone value, COUNT (cells used), NEG_COUNT (values negative in the source), and the chosen statistics. A name is suggested from the zone dataset; the suggestion can be cleared or changed.
Checked (default): NoData cells within a zone are simply skipped. Unchecked: any zone containing a NoData cell receives NULL statistics (the Esri tool's behavior with the same setting).

Which statistic to write, or All statistics (the default) for every one: Mean, Median, Standard Deviation, Minimum, Maximum, Range, the 5th and 95th Percentiles, and the 95% Confidence Interval of the mean (half-width in degrees plus lower and upper bounds in the source unit). COUNT and NEG_COUNT are always included. The mean, SD and CI are computed on the slope angles; the median, percentiles, min, max and range are order statistics and are identical either way.

param.name: slope_units
param.displayname: Slope units of the input raster

dialogReference.para: The unit of the raster's slope values: Degrees (-90 to 90), Percent slope (100 × rise/run; 45° = 100%; also called grade), Rise:run ratio, or Gradians (gons; 100 gon = 90°). Defaults automatically from the raster's geoprocessing history (DEGREE or PERCENT_RISE recorded by Esri's Slope / Surface Parameters), falling back to Degrees. Statistics are computed on the slope angles regardless of this unit and converted back for display, so the choice affects labels and validation, never the underlying mathematics.

param.name: use_absolute
param.displayname: Treat negative slopes as positive (absolute steepness)

dialogReference.para: Checked (default): the absolute value of each slope is used, giving statistics on absolute steepness. Unchecked: signs are kept, so negative (downhill) slopes can balance positive (uphill) ones in the mean -- appropriate for signed directional-pitch data. NEG_COUNT always reports how many source values were negative.

scriptExample.title: Slope Zonal Statistics as Table (Python)
scriptExample.para: Summarize a percent-slope raster by management units, all statistics, absolute steepness.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy # The .pyt ships next to the add-in; ImportToolbox registers alias "jenness". arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") arcpy.jenness.SlopeZonalStatisticsAsTable( in_zone_data=r"C:\data\project.gdb\mgmt_units", zone_field="UNIT_ID", in_raster=r"C:\data\project.gdb\slope_percent", out_table=r"C:\data\project.gdb\mgmt_units_SlopeZonal", ignore_nodata=True, statistics_type="All statistics", slope_units="Percent slope (rise/run × 100)", use_absolute=True)

dataIdInfo.idAbs: Zonal slope statistics computed in angle space: the slope-targeted sibling of Esri's Zonal Statistics as Table (https://doc.esri.com/en/arcgis-pro/latest/tool-reference/spatial-analyst/zonal-statistics-as-table.html), computed without any Spatial Analyst or Image Analyst extension. Percent slope is the tangent of the slope angle -- a convex transform -- so averaging raw percent values biases steepness statistics high; this tool converts values through the arctangent before the mean, SD, and confidence interval and converts the results back for display. Reference: Zar, J.H. 1999. Biostatistical Analysis, 4th ed. Prentice Hall (ch. 7, t-based confidence interval for a mean).
dataIdInfo.idPurp: Summarize a slope raster per zone with angle-space statistics, as a table.
